title: Super VRUN on the Genesis / Mega Drive (S0: the skeleton)
description: The Genesis port of Super VRUN (docs/projects/sega-vrun-ports-plan.md, S3: 1P and 2P, the game centred in 320 with each room's edges repeated like the WideMess version, Super VRUN's own music engine on FM + PSG, ONE shared game-logic source with the SNES and WideMess versions: the proposal is in the workspace's README.md). Today the S0 skeleton: a hello ROM (text, a frame counter, both pads read, a cursor that Left / Right move). Built with SGDK 2.11 (toolchains.json) in its live workspace PROJECTS/SuperVRUN_MD_dev (its own git, local only).

toolchain: SGDK 2.11 (m68k gcc, make, libmd), pinned in toolchains.json; Java (the machine's JDK) for SGDK's sizebnd.jar / rescomp.jar

steps.name: build
steps.note: build.ps1: SGDK's makefile.gen release (-O3, LTO) into out/, then build/supervrun_md.bin and its nm symbols; checks the 'SEGA' system name at $100.

run.note: The skeleton: Left / Right move the cursor. Lite: the .md opens in BrokenNes Lite's Genesis (UAT/entrypoints/lite-sega.ps1 -Roms <folder with md\supervrun_md.md>).

memory.what: the main loop runs every frame
Left reached the pad and moved the cursor 10 columns (16 -> 6)

scenarios.why: the hello ROM on the Genesis: it runs, draws and reads the pad

compat.what: The hello ROM on every Genesis emulator BrokenDev has (BizHawk's Genplus-gx), from power-on and the same pad script. The variables are big-endian u16: the reads take their low byte (the symbol + 1).

scenarios.what: power-on, the text, Left held 10 frames

checks.what: the main loop runs (frame_count's low byte keeps changing)

comparison.what: The cross-console comparison (S0): the port against its original, Super VRUN on the SNES (project supervrun). Tolerance (2026-11-01): the same events in order, positions within a few pixels. Filled in by S3; the skeleton maps nothing yet.

knownIssues: S0 skeleton only: the game is S3.
No hardware test on the user's Genesis flash cart yet.
